title: Characteristics of the deposition of drugs in dental biofilm
summary: There are large interindividual differences in the concentration of drugs  in biofilm. This makes it difficult to use biofilm for drug detection. To improve this, research will be conducted to determine what these concentration differences depend on. Whether it depends on the sampling site of the biofilm in the mouth or on intraindividual differences and the exposure time will be investigated in a subject study. All biofilm samples will be examined microscopically and analytically-chemically.
conditions: Basic research on deposition of drugs in oral biofilm

interventions.name: Plaque is grown in the mouth of the subjects on splints and on the teeth. The splint is regularly incubated in a solution of forensically relevant drugs (amphetamine, methamphetamine and ecstasy derivatives (MDMA, MDA, MDE), cocaine, benzoylecgonine (cocaine metabolite), morphine, codeine, 6-monoace

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-unremarkable general medical history
-Age between 18 and 65 years
-healthy according to the investigator's assessment
-In females: at least one method of contraception accepted by conventional medicine
-naturally healthy or rehabilitated dentition
-Written informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
-For women: Pregnancy
-For women: Breastfeeding
-Rejection of written consent
-Allergies to the materials used in the examination (especially plastic components)
-Non-sanitized dentition or pending dental treatment other than emergency treatment
-Intake of medications/drugs/foodstuffs that impair the detection of the test substances
-Intake of antibiotics within the last 2 months.
